[ASSISTANT_SAID] Hanukkah is also known as the Festival of Lights and commemorates the rededication of the Temple in Jerusalem during the Maccabean Revolt.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Traditional Hanukkah foods often revolve around oil, symbolizing the miracle of the oil that burned for eight days in the rededicated Temple.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested traditional Hanukkah dishes include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Latkes (לאַטקעס): Crispy potato pancakes fried in oil, served with applesauce or sour cream.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Sufganiyot (סופגניות): Jelly-filled doughnuts fried in oil.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Brisket: Slow-cooked beef served with gravy.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Challah: Traditional braided bread.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Knishes (קניש): Savory pastries filled with potatoes, meat, or cheese.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Hanukkah Gelt (חנוכה געלט): Chocolate coins wrapped in foil.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 7. Tzimmes (צימעס): Sweet stew made with carrots and dried fruits.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 8. Kugel (קוגל): Baked pudding made with noodles or potatoes.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested a simple latke recipe that serves 8-10 people, yielding about 20-25 latkes.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] Latke recipe includes:  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] - 4 large potatoes, peeled  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] - 1 large onion, finely chopped  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] - 2 eggs  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] - 1/4 cup all-purpose flour  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] - 1/2 teaspoon salt  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] - 1/4 teaspoon black pepper  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] - 1/4 teaspoon paprika  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] - Vegetable oil for frying
